# 4 Maccabees Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** Eleazar's Martyrdom

---

**1** When Eleazar stood before the tribunal and the soldiers had bound him, they commanded him once more to eat the forbidden meat.

**2** But Eleazar, as a man of noble birth and a true philosopher, not lowering himself to any disgrace, spoke out:

**3** We will not be forced so easily, Antiochus, into eating unclean food; for the law is our teacher, and we know it speaks truth.

**4** When the guards had seized him and brought him to the instruments of torture, they tore open his sides with hooks, attempting to force meat into his mouth by opening his wounds.

**5** But Eleazar did not lose his self-possession; instead, while he was being tortured, he raised his eyes toward heaven and said:

**6** You know, O God, that though I could have saved myself, I am dying in these burning torments for the sake of the law.

**7** Have mercy on your people, and be satisfied that my punishment is sufficient for them.

**8** Make my blood their cleansing, and receive my life as a ransom for their lives.

**9** After saying these words, the holy man died nobly under his torments, enduring them by the power of reason rooted in devotion.

**10** Eleazar was the first to enter the path of those who are crowned by holy martyrdom.

**11** In him we see the priest holding fast to reason while all around him his body was being destroyed.

**12** He endured his torments for the sake of the law, not because he was compelled but because he freely chose to do so.

**13** O sacred conflict! O noble wrestler of the divine law! O victory of piety over bodily passion!

**14** O Eleazar, priest and philosopher! You were not cowed by the cruelty of the tyrant nor burned into surrender by the fire of the tormentors.

**15** You were an athlete of the divine commandments, clothed in an armor of devotion that fire could not destroy, and through it you overcame the adversary.

**16** In you, O father of our nation, the law proved its sovereignty — for through holy reason you demonstrated that reason is master of the passions.

**17** O Eleazar, you did not defile your sacred mouth with the defiling food even for a moment of life, nor did you dishonor the dignity of your old age for the sake of a bodily appetite.

**18** You preserved the beauty of your holy old age by the nobility of your choices.

**19** In you, the sovereignty of reason over the passions was made completely clear.

**20** Holy and honored is the death of those who die for the sake of the law.

**21** Truly blessed are you, O Eleazar! You have been granted the imperishable prizes of immortality.

**22** For you lit a lamp of devotion for all Israel that day, and your self-mastery showed clearly what it means to put reason above pleasure.

**23** At ninety years of age you were not weakened by bodily pleasures but remained vigorous through reason.

**24** While the fire burned around him and the torturers applied their instruments, he looked steadily upward with a soul that could not be conquered.

**25** O priest clothed in the garment of philosophy! O elder devoted to the holy law! O life of the man of God faithful to the ancient ways!

**26** Through such nobility, Eleazar became the pioneer of all who die for the sake of religion.

**27** Without question, the nation's suffering was sanctified by this man's devotion, and the tyranny over it was broken.

**28** For the suffering that Eleazar endured was sufficient to make the nation holy.

**29** The king himself was thereby restrained from advancing further against the holy city.

**30** And by the nobility of his death, Eleazar became the beginning of purification for all of Israel.
